hints: Focus on what the colorimeter actually measures, absorbance is not concentration, so you must link the two graphs together.
Use the left calibration graph first to find how concentration depends on absorbance, notice that absorbance 0.5 means only 0.25 x 10^-3 mol dm^-3.
Draw a tangent to the right-hand curve at 20 s and convert its gradient in absorbance per second into concentration per second.
walkthrough:
**Use the calibration curve to link absorbance to concentration**

The left graph is a straight line through the origin. It tells you how to turn any absorbance reading into a real $\text{I}_2$ concentration.

$$\text{absorbance 0.50 corresponds to } 0.25 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$$
So concentration = $0.5 \times 10^{-3} \times$ absorbance.

**Find the gradient at 20 s on the reaction curve**

Rate means change in concentration with time, so we need the gradient of a tangent at $t = 20$ s on the right graph where absorbance is about 0.30.

A good tangent at 20 s goes roughly from absorbance 0.50 at 0 s to absorbance 0.10 at 40 s.
$$\text{gradient in absorbance} = \frac{0.10 - 0.50}{40 - 0} = -0.01 \text{ s}^{-1}$$

**Convert the absorbance change into rate**

Ignore the minus sign, rate is positive for disappearance of $\text{I}_2$. Multiply by the calibration factor.
$$\text{rate} = 0.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.01 = 5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ mol dm}^{-3} \text{ s}^{-1}$$

options.A: Correct. A tangent gradient of about 0.01 absorbance units per second converts to 5 x 10^-6 mol dm^-3 s^-1 using the 0.5 x 10^-3 calibration factor. This matches the steady fall of [I2] from about 2.5 x 10^-4 to near zero over 60 s.
options.B: Too large by a factor of 2. This comes from misreading the calibration, for example taking absorbance 0.5 as 0.5 x 10^-3 mol dm^-3 instead of 0.25 x 10^-3 mol dm^-3.
options.C: Too large by 1000 times. This is the classic power-of-ten trap where the x 10^-3 label on the concentration axis is forgotten when converting absorbance to concentration.
options.D: Too large by about 2000 times. This combines forgetting the x 10^-3 factor with misreading the calibration slope, effectively using absorbance values directly as mol dm^-3.
